changelog:
0.2.6

  • FIX header: 0.2.5 changed the reset to *:not(.bt-tool):not(.bt-tool *), which raised its specificity to 1,2,0 and made it outrank the header rules, crushing the top bar. Now wrapped in :where(), which contributes zero specificity — reset is back to 1,0,0 and still skips the quote tool.
  • FIX quote tool: BT Quote enqueues its CSS and JS from inside its own shortcode; this template never printed them, so the tool rendered as bare HTML with no styling and no JS. The portal now emits both files directly in the tab, in order (CSS, markup, config, JS), and dequeues the copies BT Quote queued so nothing loads twice.
  • Still the same files from bt-quote/assets — one tool, one pricing engine, no portal copy.

0.2.5

  • The Quote tab is now the exact same tool as the public /quote/ page — BT Quote's [bt_quick_quote], one codebase, no portal copy to drift.
  • Two reasons it came through bare before: BT Quote's stylesheet was enqueued mid-content so it landed late or not at all, and the portal reset (#bt-schedule-app *, specificity 1,0,0) outranked every class rule in it. Now the stylesheet is enqueued up front on the portal page, and the reset skips the .bt-tool subtree entirely.
  • No spacing rules duplicated into the portal — BT Quote styles its own tool, so the two stay identical automatically.

0.2.4

  • Quote tab prices again. Same card, same layout — only the values it sends changed to match BT Quote 0.3.1: garment IDs instead of generic names, "embroidery" instead of "emb", embType instead of emb_type, retail instead of garment_cost, and it reads perShirt instead of each.
  • The garment dropdown is now generated from BT Quote's own pricing tables at render time, so it can never drift from the engine again.
  • Max Colors removed — BT Quote prices full colour by location, so the dropdown never changed the number.
  • Locations capped at 3 (the engine's limit). Embroidery over the by-quote minimum shows "By Quote" instead of an error.

0.2.3

  • Quote tab restored to exactly what the snippet port shipped. 0.2.1 (swapping in BT Quote's shortcode) and 0.2.2 (CSS to compensate for it) are both reverted. The portal frontend is byte-identical to v0.2.0 again — the port stays invisible to employees.

0.2.2

  • Fix: Quote tab layout — the portal's universal CSS reset (#bt-schedule-app *) outranked BT Quote's stylesheet and flattened every margin, padding and gap in the quote tool, collapsing the cards into a run-together mess. The tool's spacing is now re-stated at matching specificity so the reset can't win.

0.2.1

  • FIX: Quote tab showed "Pricing error" and a plain form. The portal was carrying its own copy of the quote UI from the July 24 port, built against BT Quote v0.1.0. BT Quote is now v0.3.1 and its /price endpoint expects garment IDs (g5000, bc3001, supplied, custom) instead of generic labels (tshirt, hoodie), so every request came back 400 invalid_garment.
  • The Quote tab now renders BT Quote's own [bt_quick_quote] shortcode. One quote UI, maintained in one place, no drift.
  • Removed 189 lines of duplicated quote code from the portal.

0.2.0

  • Redirect module ported in from BT-Sched-5-Redirect — the /stores/ redirect portal and [bt_redirect_tab] now ship with the plugin. Deactivate the old snippet after updating.
  • Redirect tab: copy button on each URL Path row copies the full https link to the clipboard.
  • All option names, post meta keys, AJAX actions and the shortcode tag are unchanged, so existing redirect pages and click counts carry over untouched.

0.1.1

  • Stores tab: copy-to-clipboard icon beside each store's VIEW link.

0.1.0

  • Initial plugin release — full port of the BT-Sched WPCode snippets (DB + crons, REST API, [bt_schedule] frontend, head CSS).
  • Admin status page with update check, self-updater via GitHub manifest.
